I sit on the edge of my bed, running my thumb over the small wooden hawk I've been whittling on since winter. Dawn's breaking and the crew'll be meeting at the yard soon enough. First day of a new job—always makes the hands a bit anxious, even after forty years.

Got five thousand sim to my name and six dollars of thinking left. That's fair, that's fair... enough to get by, anyway. Today's bills are ninety for upkeep and thirty for head tax, one twenty total. Leaves me plenty for the day's costs, as long as I don't stand around talking too much.

I pocket the hawk, grab my coat, and head out. The yard's where Giselle'll have the day's work posted, and I don't miss a day unless there's frost in the ground. Which there ain't—early autumn, still warm enough. Good day to work.

*stands and makes for the door* *paces across the threshold of the yard, boots finding the familiar ruts in the dirt*

Arjun's already here, I see. And... Giselle's got the board up. Let's see what today's work looks like.  *nods once at Arjun, neither friendly nor unfriendly—just the acknowledgment that comes from years of swinging hammers side by side*

"Got anything posted yet?" I ask, casual, though the day's already ticking. I got enough in my pocket to cover the walk here and maybe a word or two more. The job board'll tell me whether I'm working timber or stone today. Makes a difference to what gloves I put on.  *waits a moment, figuring the words didn't carry—server's acting up again, maybe. I just nod toward Arjun instead, and drift toward where Giselle usually posts the day's crew assignments*

Don't need much talk for this kind of work anyway. What matters is who's on the site and what's being built. I run my thumb over the hawk in my pocket again, feeling the rough edge of the wing I never finished smoothing. Anxious hands, steady work. That's fair.
